title: Reactions to Alma's words
summary: After Alma finishes speaking, many believe his words and begin to repent and search the scriptures. The greater part are angry with Alma and Amulek, desire to destroy them, and seek to put them away secretly.

explicit_facts.text: After Alma finished speaking, many believed his words and began to repent and search the scriptures.
The greater part desired to destroy Alma and Amulek.
They were angry about Alma's plain words to Zeezrom and said Amulek had lied and reviled against their law, lawyers, and judges.
Angry with Alma and Amulek for testifying plainly against their wickedness, they sought to put them away secretly.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance and arrangement of the people, scriptures, and surroundings.

they sought to put them away privily.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the secret removal or destruction as having occurred.

The same unnamed people take Alma and Amulek to the place of martyrdom so they might witness the destruction of those consumed by fire.

title: Amulek asks to save them
summary: Amulek, pained by the suffering of the women and children in the fire, asks Alma whether they can exercise God's power and save them. Alma says the Spirit constrains him not to stretch forth his hand and explains that the Lord receives them in glory.

Alma said their deaths would make the judgments against the people just, and the blood of the innocent would stand as a witness against them at the last day.

title: The judge confronts them
summary: After the bodies and records are consumed, the chief judge stands before bound Alma and Amulek, strikes their cheeks, and taunts them about preaching again and their inability to save the victims. The text notes the judge followed Nehor's order and faith.

explicit_facts.text: After the bodies and records were consumed, the chief judge stood before Alma and Amulek while they were bound, struck their cheeks, and asked whether they would preach again that the people would be cast into a lake of fire and brimstone.
The judge said they had not power to save those cast into the fire and struck them again, asking what they had to say for themselves.
The judge was after the order and faith of Nehor, who slew Gideon.

unspecified_visual_details: The judge's appearance and the specific visual state of the consumed bodies and records.
